ROUND 2 performance verdict: PASS-WITH-NOTES (final round, C34).
Subject: pr:322
Head: eebc7023719fcdf1df3edc8cd14e83955fb9a5bb
Answers: 01a1fedb-72fa-7b11-b607-953fc9cb8967

No new loop, poll, timer or launch site is added by the F270 R2 delta. The sender-less ledger guard adds a constant empty-string check; a refused ack does not schedule a daemon retry. The new control-refusal replay does add history-query work and one durable event per refused-control acknowledgement. No normal-use resource-cost breach is demonstrated here. This cost verdict does not clear the separate correctness/security reviews or claim that every malformed generic delivery has a bounded lifetime.

Control admission / refusal cost:
- arrive_control previously made one latest_matching_message call. R2 makes ONE call when its sender's refusal key is found, or TWO when absent (the second is the legacy delivery.outcome lookup). Thus the incremental call count versus R1 is zero on a hit and one on a miss, not an unconditional extra call followed by another extra call. Each real-store call adds a schema PRAGMA and its SELECT. Both run under the existing global socket_delivery_order mutex.
- The <len>:<sender>:<msg_id> key is stored in JSON, not in a message-key index. Both calls seek the recipient's (seat, kind) spine index, then filter json_extract(payload,'$.msg_id') while walking that history in reverse sequence order. With R target control-refusal facts, a first-probe miss/old hit may visit R facts across all senders; the fallback can additionally visit the target's delivery.outcome history. A same-sender new key is not a point-key seek merely because its spelling is unambiguous.
- Exact-source SQL on schema50, SQLite3.54.1, an in-memory cohort of 2,000 control refusals: oldest key 12,042 VM instructions; newest 28; missing other-sender key 12,015. EXPLAIN uses spine_by_seat_kind (seat=?, kind=?). This is candidate-work proof, not elapsed-time or live CPU measurement. Receipt: files/pr322-r2-control-cost.log.
- A refused-control acknowledgement now adds ONE EventBus.publish of delivery.control-refused before the existing delivery.outcome publication and plain queue ack. On the real store this is an additional schema read, owned write transaction/INSERT/COMMIT, event clone/broadcast and JSON encoding/storage of the key, sender and refusal outcome. The two fact writes are separate transactions, under the existing native/socket ordering locks. Repeating a failed acknowledgement can repeat publication; there is no new autonomous writer loop.

Sender-less ack / stuck-claim cost:
- ack_delivery already reads dedupe_sender and tentatively UPDATEs the running job to done inside its write transaction. record_delivered now rejects an empty sender before its held-flag/ledger/retention queries. Failure rolls back the UPDATE; no new wildcard ledger row is committed, and the job remains running. The added successful-path guard performs no SQL, roster traversal, JSON parse or process launch.
- There is no timer attached to that error or new server ack-retry task. Expiry transitions occur lazily in claim_inner when another claim pass for those kinds runs. A running row continues to occupy its serial_key until an applicable claim/recovery/explicit operation changes it. The same recipient's other pending work is blocked during that running interval; other serial keys remain eligible.
- Distinguish readers: OMP/Pi use claim_extension, normally a 60s extension claim lease, with the existing three-expiry terminal park and the Working renewal BRAKE. Busy renewal/explicit claim heartbeats can extend that interval. Ordinary queue.claim (including Copilot native/manual readers) uses the configured ordinary lease, 300s by default, and does NOT increment the extension lease-expiration budget. Body claims can recycle across later claim passes without a fixed total attempt cap; controls fail terminally on expiry instead. No consumer means no claim-driven reaper; a separate native-receiver lapse may still park the job through existing F260 reconciliation.
- Existing native wait passes wake on recipient events, next-due work and at most the 15s empty-wait backstop; the client has its existing 250ms-to-5s retry backoff. These are inherited triggers, not new R2 polling. The stock Copilot client rejects an empty sender in messageFromClaim before injection/ack and holds receiving, aborting its receive/heartbeat loops. A direct store/raw ack failure is not proof that the stock client repeatedly sends bad acks. At HTTP, a store/queue Adapter error maps to 500, so clients that choose to retry errors can generate additional request/rollback work; no server-side attempt-rate cap is introduced.
- Normal specialized delivery enqueue/claim paths already require a sender. The new test deliberately uses generic enqueue({}), and then explicitly disposes of the running row with a plain ack; that test proves ledger refusal, NOT autonomous retirement or a universal queue-cost bound. The correctness reviewer was sent the generic-versus-extension distinction.

R1 cost-table corrections:
- Accepted: settlement is explicitly not O(1); JSON sender parsing/index maintenance is named; three expiry subprobes are separate from the ledger's current/legacy point-key pair; index occupied-page figures are snapshots, not ceilings.
- Migration0050 and the earlier expiry/settlement query source are unchanged by R2. The table correctly attributes release store-open receipts to c0cae51: 0.796449s and 0.576329s on clean copies (46,061 jobs; 77,452 ledger rows). These receipts were independently verified in R1 and retained. They are not a live bounce, a worst-case bound or a timing of eebc702; the main merge includes the independently reviewed #321 pool-hook change. No copy/build/migration rerun was needed for this three-line writer guard and control replay delta.
- #316/#318/#320/#321 changes arrived through main and are not new F270 launch/timer sites.

notes_owed:
1. new (C34 follow-up, nonblocking): price control replay as 1/2 total history-filtering calls (0/+1 incremental versus R1), plus one durable delivery.control-refused publication per refusal ack. The existing cost row's "seek" does not bound JSON candidate work; a message-keyed spine lookup is a possible measured follow-up, not a new timer.
2. new (C34 follow-up, nonblocking): do not describe a refused generic/native claim as automatically retired after three expiries. The three-expiry rule is extension-claim-specific, expiry is claim-driven, and a stopped reader can leave a running serial-key occupant until other recovery. Retain these limits in any malformed-claim cost/lifecycle claim; correctness/security own normal-use reachability and disposition.

Sources at the exact head:
delivery/mod.rs:1094-1148,2170-2498,2698-2843,3177-3184; store/spine.rs:267-276,397-419; events/mod.rs:78-98; store/queue.rs:103-280,301-335,744-767,1837-1890,1957-1959; store/tests/message_sender.rs:79-127; core/config.rs:210; http/mod.rs:3513-3542,3937-3951; .copilot/extensions/pij/store.mjs:18-19,1056-1071,1756-1831,2307-2313. Existing F260 receiver parking and the 15s backstop are unchanged.

Validation and limitations:
- just pr-freeze 322: FINAL at the full head, CLEAN, five latest checks passed; migration50 is the sole new migration, main highest49.
- git diff --check c0cae51..HEAD: passed; detached review worktree clean.
- Exact-head CI44922138243 completed/success; successful rust-test job136900289680 uploaded artifact14714272344. Independently parsed JUnit: 2,827 cases, zero failures/errors/skipped. All six selected sender/refusal/migration/expiry/settlement cases and all six spawn-site guards ran and passed.
- The new no_ack_writes_a_sender_less_ledger_row and a_refused_control_never_answers_another_senders_same_id cases, plus a_refusal_recorded_before_f270_still_replays, are explicitly present and passed. Independent reviewer probes and S1/C1-C3 mutants were not rerun by this performance seat; no claim to reproduce their results.
- harness boot --json: ready=false (missing vitest). harness checks --quick --json: exit1, eight dependency/ambient-tool failures; pij-skill/native/SDK pass, heavy Rust/route/smoke skipped. Local gate is not green; exact-head CI is separate C25 proof.
- No product edits, Rust builds, production DB reads/writes, bounce, working-seat mutation or live retry experiment in R2. Only the owned CI download is temporary; cost logs and verdict evidence remain in session artifacts. Holding performance/322 until merge.

Policy/brakes: sender identity and sender-specific refusal replay decide a different outcome and are policies. The sender-less writer rejection, legacy wildcard replay and settled-expiry shortcut only spare/admit less work: brakes. No retention policy or claim-retry timer was added.

Harness lesson / magicWand: distinguish a message-key spelling from a message-key index, and keep a small cost receipt for control-refusal lookup misses plus the extra fact write. A lifecycle proof should identify the actual reader's claim mode rather than borrow another mode's retry budget.
